# Tuṇḍilajātaka (Ja 388)

**ID:** Ja 388  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Tuṇḍilajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul5.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul5.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tuṇḍilajātaka* (Ja 388) is a birth story preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Pali canon. Set at Jetavana, the discourse is delivered by the Buddha concerning a monk who lived in intense fear of death (*maraṇabhīruko*) [Fausböll 1883].

In the narrative of the past, the Bodhisatta is born as a boar named Mahātuṇḍila, living with his younger brother Cullatuṇḍila [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. When Cullatuṇḍila is about to be slaughtered by thirty men, he flees to his elder brother, quaking in terror [Cowell 1897]. Mahātuṇḍila comforts him and delivers two verses expounding the Dhamma: because they have been fattened for their meat, escape is impossible; instead, Cullatuṇḍila should plunge into the spotless pool to wash away all stains and obtain an unwaning fragrance [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. In the closing identification (*samodhāna*), the fearful monk is identified as Cullatuṇḍila, Ānanda as the king, the gathered assembly as the Buddha's assembly, and Mahātuṇḍila as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883]. The *Dhammapada* commentary also references this sermon, noting that thirty companions were swiftly converted and attained arahantship because in this previous life they had observed the five precepts after hearing Mahātuṇḍila's preaching [Burlingame 1921a; Burlingame 1921b; Weragoda Sarada 1993].

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, Jātaka together with Its Commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Pali verse text, prose framing story, and the closing samodhāna.
- [Cowell 1897] E. B. Cowell, The Jātaka, Vol. 3 (1897) — English translation of the narrative episode and verses.
- [Burlingame 1921a] Eugene W. Burlingame, Buddhist Legends, Vol. 1 (1921) — Dhammapada commentary references and synopses citing the Tuṇḍilajātaka.
- [Burlingame 1921b] Eugene W. Burlingame, Buddhist Legends, Vol. 2 (1921) — Dhammapada commentary story on verse 65 citing Mahā Tuṇḍila's sermon in the Tuṇḍila Jātaka.
- [Weragoda Sarada 1993] Weragoda Sarada Thero, Treasury of Truth: Illustrated Dhammapada (1993) — Discussion of the Dhammapada story referencing the instruction of Venerable Tuṇḍila.
